x: Trower was our first runner home in 10th position (29.08), G.

Ron Linstead had received an injury during a training run, G.Goode had a severe cold and Frank Wright was unable to get leave. However the rest of the lads had a good try but could do no better than 20th out of the 24 teams.

In the 1 mile Virr of T.V.H. struck out early and was followed by Geoff Goode for a couple of laps. On the last lap Jon Burr passed the latter and if he had had a baton might have also caught his rival of the Brighton road.

Brian Barry of the promoting club won the mile in 4m. 11s. with Cliff Roffey 3rd and Geoff Goode 4th. The relay proved a very convincing win for our very scratch team of Denis Merrett, Ian Forrester, Percy Luxon and Mal Ash.

Geoff Goode was entrusted, in the absence of more prominent "A" team members, with the 7th stage but had to give way to Finchley, Essex Beagles and Herne Hill who had come into the race through Ron Clark.

…Ron Clarke, but experience soon prevailed,and Ron steadily pulled away.A game but very tired Newall handed his baton to Geoff Goode at "The Castle" 3mins behind T.V.H and 1¼mins behind H.H.H but still in 3rd position.…
Ex-members, Geoff Goode and Steve Charlton were seen running for their new clubs. Semi-retired Bagnall would have been our third scoring man with his 56th place!!
Promising Geoff Goode took the Junior Mile in 4:31. Our Nigerian performer E.Bone took the High Jump from P.Luxon who had previously done the double with both the Javelin and Long Jump.
